title: Fragmentation Mapper — Token tiling export probe
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Prototype a compact, export-first token-level cost view called 'Fragmentation Mapper' that surfaces per-invocation token tiling, role-aware debit lanes, and export choreography. Goal is to let engineering and finance stakeholders quickly isolate cost hotspots at the token-fragment level, iterate on pricing presets, and export attribution-ready payloads for downstream billing or analytics pipelines.

Background: We have several large design tickets exploring token-attribution UIs focused on heatmaps and ledgers. This probe explores a different interaction model — tile-based fragmentation that groups tokens by attribution dimension (route/model/role/route-variant) and prioritizes export and sanity-check workflows: CSV/NDJSON export with ratecard mapping and role scoping. This is intended for power users who need high-fidelity export artifacts for chargeback or audit.

Scope: 1) Single-screen prototype showing a compact token-tiling canvas + side rail with pricing preset controls. 2) Export flow (CSV, NDJSON, Parquet stub) with configurable fields: token-range, prompt-id, model-variant, cost-line, ratecard-applied, and actor-id. 3) Role-aware filters + permission hints (showing which tokens are visible to current user). 4) Micro-presets for pricing (per-token base rates, surcharge bands for long prompts, quantization multipliers) and a preview of how presets change exported totals. 5) Lightweight inline validation for sampling vs deterministic attribution (explain margin of error).

Deliverables: - High-fidelity Figma prototype (desktop + narrow window) - Clickable export flow (CSV / NDJSON) - Spec sheet for engineering (API contract for export, pagination, performance constraints) - Usability script and 6-user moderated test checklist - Edge-case notes for private deployments (VPC export endpoints, audit log hooks)

Acceptance criteria: - Product can reproduce per-route and per-role totals within ±0.5% for common workloads. - Export includes schema header and stable keys for downstream systems. - Prototype demonstrates quick path to export from selected tile(s) in 2 clicks. - PM and Eng accept the export contract and sign off on performance SLO for on-demand exports.

Constraints & trade-offs: - Precision vs UI complexity: showing exact per-token model internals (kv cache hits, attention pruning) would overwhelm users; we surface sampled metrics with clear confidence bands. - Performance: on-demand token-level exports are potentially expensive; design includes async export + notification and a streaming small-preview option. - Permissioning: role-aware scoping must be simple in the UI and map cleanly to existing RBAC (see dependencies).

Open questions: - Default export schema: do we include raw token text in exports by default or keep it opt-in for PII concerns? (security team flagged opt-in). - Pricing presets: should there be a global org-level preset and per-route override? PM prefers both; prototyping both.

Metrics of success: - 80% of pilot users can generate a validated export within first session without help. - Exports reduce manual reconciliation errors in finance by >30% in pilot accounts. - Feature leads to at least one Dedicated customer upgrade in pilot cohort due to audit/export requirements.

Notes for engineering: See PR #2345 for early API contract draft. Eng team flagged batch-export should support chunking with a 30s SLO for preview and background job for full exports. Include rate-limits and quota checks in spec.
